cards.front: Recall a key point about Hand and Machine Stitching
cards.back: Running stitch and back stitch are basic construction stitches; chain, satin and French knots are decorative stitches with distinct visual qualities.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Hand and Machine Stitching
cards.back: Free-motion machine embroidery drops the feed dogs, allowing you to draw with thread — it requires practice to control speed and direction.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Hand and Machine Stitching
cards.back: Appliqué attaches fabric shapes to a background fabric — it can be fused, pinned or stitched in place before edge-stitching.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Hand and Machine Stitching
cards.back: Patchwork and piecing join fabric pieces edge-to-edge; accuracy in cutting and seam allowance is essential for flat, even results.

cards.front: What should you know about textile design exam tips?
cards.back: Show PROCESS — include practice samples alongside developed pieces. Annotate with stitch NAMES. Demonstrate TENSION control — loose, even stitches show technical skill. Compare hand and machine approaches.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Machine embroidery is just about following the machine's built-in patterns. Correct: Free-motion machine embroidery is a CREATIVE technique where YOU control the stitching direction and speed — the machine only moves the needle up and down. It is like drawing with thread, requiring hand-eye coordination and practice.
Create a stitched sample sheet showing at least six different hand stitches and two machine embroidery techniques. Annotate each with the stitch name, its properties and a possible application.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Hand and Machine Stitching
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Hand and Machine Stitching using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.
